title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered 29, from a French draft of an étale-cohomology exposé. It has typewriter corrections and a handwritten reference '(VIII.5.5)'. It is inserted among Grothendieck's crystalline scribbles; the neighbouring pages, on crystalline and Hodge fibre functors and torsors, are unrelated. The content is the standard proof of a base-change compatibility for the local cohomology sheaves R^q i^! along a smooth divisor. This is the setting of relative cohomological purity and smooth base change, as in SGA 4 XVI/XIX and SGA 4½ 'Cycle'.

Step 1 (the R^1 j_* computation). Setup: i: Y -> X is a closed immersion with open complement j: U -> X, and g, u are base-change maps. One computes the stalk at a geometric point x̄ of R^1 j_* g^*F. It equals H^1(Ũ, g̃^*F̃), where Ũ is the punctured strict henselisation (the Milnor-fibre-like local object). Ū is the tame Kummer cover of Ũ obtained by adjoining all n-th roots of a local equation, n prime to the residue characteristics. Ū is 'strongly 1-acyclic for L', so H^1(Ū, F) = 0 and H^0(Ū, F) = H^0(S̃, F̃). The low-degree Hochschild–Serre sequence for the Galois cover Ū/Ũ, with group G = lim Z/nZ ≅ Ẑ'(1) (tame inertia), then gives (R^1 j_* g^*F)_x̄ ≅ H^1(G, H^0(S̃, F̃)). Both H^0(S̃, F̃) and G commute trivially with the base change S̄ -> S. Hence R^1 j_* g^*F commutes with base change.

Step 2 (the general case). For F of L-torsion, the theorem is restated as a base-change isomorphism u'^*(R^q i^!) g^*F ≅ (R^q i'^!) g'^* u^*F for every q. The case q = 2 is already done; it is essentially the cycle class / purity isomorphism R^2 i^! Z/n ≅ Z/n(-1). An induction argument from an earlier (3.7) gives the result for all q when F = Z/n. A dévissage, citing (VIII.5.5) and a lemma on the next typed page, reduces general L-torsion F to that case.
errors: First displayed line writes H^q(Ũ, g̃^*F̃) where H^1 is meant, as the following lines make clear.
Notation drifts between bars and tildes: H^0(Ū, ḡ^*F̄) ≈ H^0(S̃, F̃) mixes the Ū- and S̃-levels. Harmless, but sloppy.
G should be the prime-to-residue-characteristic profinite completion lim_{(n,p)=1} Z/n (≅ Ẑ'(1)), not the full lim Z/nZ. The restriction is implicit in L.

ideas.what: Computing R^1 j_* along a smooth divisor via the tame Kummer tower and low-degree Hochschild–Serre, with tame inertia group Ẑ'(1)
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of tame nearby/vanishing cohomology; first step of relative cohomological purity

ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. XVI and XIX; SGA 1 XIII

ideas.what: Base change for local cohomology sheaves R^q i^! for a smooth pair, by induction from q=2 and dévissage
ideas.modern_name: Relative purity / compatibility of i^! with base change for smooth pairs

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray typed page of a standard SGA 4-style purity/base-change proof, probably Artin's French draft given the anglicisms ('il est évident de l'argument'). It is filed among unrelated crystalline notes. The mathematics is fully standard and published; only the archival placement is mildly curious.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the image indeed reads H^q(Ũ, g̃^*F̃), but H^1 is meant.
'(R^q i_!)' and '(R^q i'_!)' should be read as R^q i^! and R^q i'^! (upper shriek, cohomology with supports); the image shows a superscript '!' on i'.
'(VIII.5.5)' is a handwritten insertion; the struck words before 'qu'il est' are typewriter overstrikes ('xxxx').
G = lim_n Z/nZ = G(Ū/Ũ): the struck-out alternative was G(Ū/Ũ) × G(Ū̄/Ū).
The '67' in the bottom-left margin is the archive folio number; '29' is the typescript page number.
